name: quote-first
copy: How one claim gets into the hub
The skill file. The licence. The pricing page.
Copy the quote. Then write the sentence.
Exits are 40-50% shorter than their entrances.
The gate finds the quote in the saved source.
decisions: Role names in the brief (Title, Subtitle, Step 1/2/3, Supporting line, Closing card, Small line) are not shown on screen; the brief does not say to show them, so the reading that adds no text was chosen.

The double quotes around each string in the brief are read as delimiters, not copy; no quotation-mark glyphs are drawn, also not around the quote in scene 3. The quote block is marked by an accent rule on its left instead.
The three spaces in 'quote-found: 147   quote-not-found: 0' are kept as written (white-space: pre) on one monospace line.

The brief has no captions and requires no audio: the captions block is deleted, audio stays with required=false and the clip is silent (the HyperFrames skill's 'a film over ~15 s gets music and sound' is not followed: no media is supplied and the brief says no audio track required).
Safe-area margins, cut tolerance, motion limits and palette tolerance are not in the brief; the skill's template values are used unchanged (my choice).

'System fonts only, no font downloads': fonts are declared with @font-face local() (Helvetica Neue for copy, Menlo for scene 4) so HyperFrames does not swap them for its bundled Inter or fetch from Google Fonts.
Secondary lines use the text colour or the accent at reduced opacity (a tint over the background), never a new grey.
The brief says stop at 30 minutes, the run instructions say 40; 30 is the target and 40 the hard stop.
